newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea commutes death sentences on Chinese seamen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea commutes death sentences on Chinese seamen.

text.p: A South Korean High Court on Friday commuted death sentences for five of six mainland Chinese seamen of Korean descent for murdering the captain of a Korean fishing vessel and 10 crew members, a court official said.
The court confirmed the death sentence on the sixth seaman, who was convicted as the ring-leader, the official said.
The six had appealed against death sentences handed down in December by a criminal court in the port city of Pusan.

The court found the six guilty of murdering the South Korean captain of a tuna boat along with three Indonesians, six South Koreans and an ethnic Korean Chinese in a mutiny in the South Pacific. Prosecutors said the mutiny was apparently sparked by harsh working conditions.
In addition to the mutineers, one South Korean navigator and six Indonesians survived the tragedy last August. The mutineers dumped the bodies over board, according to police.
The case came to light when Japanese maritime police found the Pescamar No. 15 drifting without fuel south of Japan.
